bullets.title: FOMC holds at 3.75-4%, hawkish inflation language keeps December hike live
bullets.body: Fed held rates unchanged at 3.75-4.0% with hawkish statement on inflation; two dissenters called for a rate hike. December hike remains ~85% priced; futures dialing back the third move for next year. US 10-year yield down 4bps to 4.99% overnight.

bullets.title: MSFT beats hard on Azure (48% growth), guides 49-50%; FCF positive vs peers
bullets.body: Microsoft posted F1Q27 revenue $92.3B (+19% YoY, 2% beat) and non-GAAP EPS $4.89 (+27%, 3% beat). Azure accelerated to 48% YoY with Q2 guided at 49-50% cc, beating consensus by ~4pts as demand exceeds supply. Copilot daily users +50% QoQ, operating margins at 25-year highs, and critically MSFT generated positive FCF — a contrast to GOOGL/META/AMZN. Stock +4-5% AH; multiple sell-side PT raises (GS $700, Piper $650, DADCO $650).

bullets.title: GOOGL misses Search by ~300bps vs consensus, stock -10-11% AH; capex trajectory alarming
bullets.body: Alphabet Q3 Search revenue grew only 12% vs Street at ~14.7-15%, with EBIT $40.1B well below expectations; YouTube and GCP also missed. GCP grew +103% YoY and backlog reached $514-561B, but quarterly CapEx hit $51.4B resulting in negative $9.1B FCF. FY26 capex guide maintained at $195-205B with a "significant increase" flagged for FY27 — buy-side circling $350-375B. AI mode queries depressing monetization; Search now <50% of revenue for first time. Multiple downgrades/PT cuts (Piper to $345, Citi to $375, Citizens to market perform).

bullets.title: MSFT raises ~$25B in first IG bond offering since 2017 to fund AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Microsoft filed a 10-part notes offering via JPMorgan, UBS, and Wells Fargo, with Bloomberg reporting the raise targets approximately $25B — its first investment-grade bond sale in over nine years. The move underscores the capital intensity of AI infrastructure buildout even for cash-generative hyperscalers.

bullets.title: AI financing stress bifurcating: hyperscalers manageable, leveraged operators (CRWV) at risk
bullets.body: Barclays and DA Davidson both flag growing external funding needs across Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon as AI CapEx accelerates. Leveraged operators like CoreWeave face heightened financing vulnerability amid rising borrowing costs; Cipher Mining's difficulties triggered broader sector selling. Only ~60% of surveyed investors expect financing constraints to become a problem — Barclays characterizes this as a "denial phase." Oracle is shifting to vendor financing and customer-provided chips as evidence of tightened capital conditions.

bullets.title: AI/momentum trade under pressure: software sector -3%, cyber stocks -26% to -52%
bullets.body: FTNT collapsed -26% after product growth decelerated to 37% (from 52% in Q2) and services missed; NOW fell -18% on cRPO guide of +18.5% vs Street +20%. The broader software sector is down ~3% on the session as the AI theme sold amid defensive bias. Cyber stocks are reportedly down ~52% over the trailing 90 days on valuation reset. NDX futures -104bps vs RTY futures +36bps reflects rotation pressure.

bullets.title: Retail flows into leveraged equity ETFs at records; call buying remains depressed
bullets.body: JPMorgan AM notes retail inflows into leveraged equity ETFs are at record levels post-deleveraging, but call option buying among retail remains depressed — creating potential upside catalyst if sentiment re-emerges into year-end. The AI/momentum trade is currently under pressure, reinforcing defensive bias across the tape.

bullets.title: ORCL Investor Day eases AI capex crowding-out fears; stock +11%
bullets.body: Oracle's Investor Day clarified only ~$20B incremental capex needed through FY30 to reach 10GW capacity (vs. consensus $171B total estimate), with FCF expected to turn positive in 2HFY28 and reach $30B+ in FY29. Updated LT revenue target raised to $225B+ (35% 5-yr CAGR). The capex step-down from FY27-28 peaks is the key relief valve for cloud multiples across the sector.

bullets.title: MRVL in advanced talks to acquire LITE in ~$90B+ AI optics megadeal
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports Marvell is near a deal to acquire Lumentum — potentially one of the 10 largest tech deals ever given LITE's $83B market cap (up 900%+ since early 2025, trading at 30x LTM revenue). Strategic rationale: combining MRVL's optical DSPs with LITE's lasers/photonics for vertical integration in AI connectivity; optical interconnect is ~50% of MRVL's FY31 revenue target. Key risks: MRVL only has $3.9B cash so deal would be largely stock-based (dilution); MRVL DSP customers compete directly with LITE; NVDA has a long-term purchase commitment and equity stake in LITE. MRVL -10.9%, LITE +6-10% on the news.

bullets.title: Samsung validates tight memory supply into CY28; DRAM/HBM pricing up ~20% in 3Q
bullets.body: Samsung expects demand to exceed industry supply for several years, targeting 60-70% capacity under long-term agreements; CY27 capex focused on clean room space that won't generate meaningful bit growth until CY28. DRAM prices rose ~20% and NAND high-teens in 3Q with server ASPs leading. Samsung is ramping HBM4E in CY27 and has signed LTAs with 10 customers. Read-through supports MU and memory supply thesis.

bullets.title: Semiconductors driving ~2/3 of S&P 500 earnings growth; AI accounts for ~75% of that
bullets.body: Barclays notes semiconductors are expected to drive approximately two-thirds of S&P 500 earnings growth next year, with AI exposure accounting for roughly 75% of semiconductor contribution. SOX index has retraced 8% since earnings season preview began; consensus EPS revisions moderating (3%/8% vs 7%/10% in Q2). Crowded long/short positioning amplifies rotation risks despite subdued index volatility.

bullets.title: Data center NIMBY opposition becoming a material risk factor for AI infrastructure buildout
bullets.body: JPMorgan AM flags that opposition tracking to data center siting is becoming a material risk factor for AI infrastructure buildout timelines and capital deployment. This is an emerging constraint alongside supply-chain and financing pressures.

bullets.title: KLAC strong beat/raise reinforces healthy semicon equipment demand; WFE outlook $200B+ in 2027
bullets.body: KLAC Q1 revenue $4.14B (13.1% QoQ) beat expectations; Q2 guided to $4.7B. Management expects mid-$150B WFE in 2026 stepping up to $200B+ in 2027. Citi cut target to $275 on softer near-term WFE outlook, but overall semicon equipment demand remains healthy. ENTG separately delivered a major beat-and-raise: Sep-Q sales $1.01B vs guidance $905-935M, Dec-Q guided $1.03-1.06B vs Street $961M.

bullets.title: DoorDash acquiring Instacart for ~$17B; could close end-2027 or H1 2028
bullets.body: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart (CART) for $65/share (~$17B equity value) per Goldman Sachs and Jefferies reporting. Deal expected to close end of 2027 or H1 2028. CART was +3.4% post-close on deal speculation.

bullets.title: S&P futures -0.23-0.4%; Nasdaq bearish trend per Hedgeye; COMPQ range 25,811-26,814
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures down ~18-20pts (0.23-0.4%) Thursday morning after mixed Wednesday close. Hedgeye flags COMPQ as bearish trend (range 25,811-26,814) while SPX remains bullish (7,625-7,786). RUT futures +36bps vs NDX -104bps suggests intraday rotation into small caps. WTI down 0.5% to ~$101.41 on diplomatic overtures toward Iran.

bullets.title: ECB leadership transition: Lagarde departs Feb 7, 2026; continuity most likely outcome
bullets.body: ECB President Lagarde confirmed early departure on February 7, 2026, presiding over two more policy meetings. With Schnabel leaving January 3 and Lane departing May 31, EU leaders may make all three ECB appointments simultaneously. Continuity is the base case as no clear political pressure for hawkish or dovish shift exists.

bullets.title: Euro area confidence deteriorated in October; consumers flagging price pressure and financial stress
bullets.body: European Commission ESI fell 0.6pt to 96.9 in October, with consumer sentiment -1.1pt and retail -1.5pt posting the largest sectoral declines. France drove consumer deterioration; Germany ESI -0.7pt. Signals remain consistent with ~1.5% annualized Q4 expansion, but consumers report rising price pressures and deteriorated personal financial situations.

bullets.title: AMZN reports after close today; AWS margins expected low 40s with 46% 2027 target
bullets.body: UBS raised Amazon PT to $348 (from $318) ahead of today's post-close report. AWS operating margins expected in the low 40s for Q3, with UBS modeling 46% in 2027 vs. 38% consensus. EPS expected $1.97 on revenue $202.22B per StreetAccount. INTC also reports today with CQ3 revenue approaching $17B and CQ4 guided ~$17.5B.

bullets.title: NOW cRPO deceleration (-21% in Q3, guided +18.5% in Q4) triggers -18% AH; AI ACV target raised to $1.7B
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 revenue $4.11B was only marginally above consensus, but cRPO of +20.3% disappointed and Q4 guidance of +18.5% was well below Street's +20% — driving the stock -18% after hours. AI ACV grew +65% and the 2026 target was raised to $1.7B (+70% from year-start), but accounting/timing items including carve-out of deployment work from subscription revenue and early Q3 renewals clouded the read. Management guiding for stronger AI acceleration in 2027.
